judgments.title: Wong Teik Heng v TENAGA NASIONAL BERHAD
judgments.catchwords: 1. In Malaysia, electricity is ordinarily supplied and consumed before payment is made. The electricity meter is therefore more than a measuring device. It is the means by which electricity consumption is measured and translated into charges payable by the consumer. When a meter is tampered with or its proper recording of electricity consumption is interfered with, electricity may continue to be consumed without that consumption being accurately recorded. 2. The present dispute arises under the Electricity Supply Act 1990. Section 37 of the Electricity Supply Act 1990 creates offences relating, amongst others, to dishonest interference with or tampering of electricity meters and the dishonest prevention of such meters from duly recording electricity consumption. The Act also provides, under section 38, for the recovery by the licensee of loss of revenue arising from the relevant offences. 3. In particular, section 38(3) permits the licensee to require the consumer to pay for the loss of revenue due to an offence committed under section 37(1), (3) or (14), whilst section 38(5) provides for the recovery of the amount by civil action. 4. The present proceedings concern such a civil claim. The Respondent, as Plaintiff in the Sessions Court, sought to recover its alleged loss of revenue arising from the meter tampering. The Respondent was therefore required to establish its claim on a balance of probabilities. 5. The Respondent succeeded before the learned Sessions Court Judge. The learned Sessions Court Judge found, amongst others, that the Appellant was the registered consumer in respect of the relevant electricity supply and allowed the Respondent’s claim in the sum of RM697,164.75. 6. It is against that decision that the present appeal is brought.

judgments.catchwords: 1. This is the Plaintiffs’ application in Enclosure 12 for discovery against the Defendant pursuant to Order 24 of the Rules of Court 2012. He submits that the discovery sought is excessive and is not necessary for the fair disposal of the action or for saving costs. 6.
